body.statement: For each \(s\in\mathcal S\), under \(q_n=\lfloor\min(n,m)^{1/5}\rfloor\), replacement of \(M_s\), \(\mu_s\), \(\alpha_s\), and \(\tau\) by \(\widehat M_s\), \(\widehat\mu_s^{\mathrm{post}}\), \(\widehat\alpha_s\), and \(\widehat\tau_s\) in the fitted influence scores is asymptotically negligible for Bartlett estimation: \(\widehat\Omega_{\psi,s}\to_{P_n}\Omega_{\psi,s}\), \(\widehat\Omega_{v,s}\to_{P_n}\Omega_{v,s}\), and \(\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}\to_{P_n}V_s\). Moreover, \(\Pr_{P_n}\{\min_{s\in\mathcal S}\widehat V_s^{\mathrm{conv}}\geq\nu/2\}\to1\).
body.justification: This lemma certifies that the concrete same-sample Bartlett standard error consistently studentizes each role coordinate without requiring inversion of the stacked covariance.
body.gap: Andrews gives kernel HAC consistency for observed score arrays, while the conventional proximal interval requires uniform control of fitted bridge-Jacobian and ATT replacement in two role-specific score arrays.
body.consumer: It makes the conventional selected-Gaussian coverage functional operational from the observed panel.
